subject: Contract amendment: add EU + APAC reserved pools, throughput SLAs
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@acme-retail.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Contract amendment: adding EU + APAC reserved pools (renewal window)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our call, Acme is planning to renew the Dedicated commitment this quarter and expand into two regional pools: an EU reserved pool for EU storefronts and an APAC pool to lower latency for your SEA customers. To recap the ask we discussed: 

- Add 8x reserved A100-equivalent GPUs in EU (Frankfurt region) and 6x in APAC (Singapore) as separate pools.
- Throughput guarantee: baseline of 70 concurrent sessions across the EU pool and 50 across APAC, with a 95th-percentile tail latency SLO of <180ms for 512-token requests.
- Failover behavior: cross-region fallback to US pooled capacity for burst events; failover window and RTO to align with your procurement needs.
- Term: align expansion with your upcoming 12-month renewal; we proposed amortized billing for the incremental nodes to smooth cash flow.

I'm looping in Karthik and Neha from Solutions to confirm the config and Marissa for legal/pricing approvals. If this matches what you expect, we'll prepare an amendment and SOW for signature (DocuSign).

Next steps I propose:
1) Karthik to confirm sizing and throughput guardrails (today)
2) Redwood sends draft amendment + SOW (by EOD Monday)
3) Procurement review and signature (target: two weeks)

Sophie — any adjustments to the numbers/timeline? Also please share the procurement contact if different from this thread.

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Attachment: Reserved_Nodes_Pricing_Table.xlsx (pricing sketch)

From: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@acme-retail.com>

Cc: Procurement Team <procure@acme-retail.com>, Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@eurodata.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Oct 2026 14:05:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Contract amendment: adding EU + APAC reserved pools (renewal window)

Jordan —

This looks aligned with our expectations. A few clarifications from procurement and engineering: 

- Can we set the EU pool to be available in FRA-1 specifically? We operate in that region for data residency reasons.
- The 95th %-ile latency target of <180ms is acceptable if measurements are from edge-to-edge (client -> Redwood -> model) for 512-token prompts; we therefore need instrumentation and a shared dashboard.
- Pricing: procurement prefers a monthly amortized line item rather than a lump-sum up front. Please attach an amortization schedule.

Procurement contact: procure@acme-retail.com (copied). Liam (CC) will validate networking and routing constraints on our side.

If you can send a draft amendment + SOW that calls out FRA-1 region, amortized billing, and the dashboard link, we can route internally.

— Sophie
Sophie Lambert
Head of AI Product | Acme Retail

Jordan / Neha —

Quick technical/readout notes based on Sophie's asks: 

1) FRA-1 availability: confirmed we can pin the EU pool to FRA-1 (we'll set deployment affinity).
2) Node sizing: 8x A100-equivalent EU pool + 6x APAC (SGP) is fine; recommend we add 1x hot spare per region for live failover (so 9 and 7). That gives you ~12% headroom and simplifies maintenance windows.
3) Throughput SLA: baseline caps map to instance concurrency; to guarantee 70/50 concurrency we need an autoscaling buffer and a soft-preempt policy. Draft SLA language attached — see Latency-SLA-Draft.docx.
4) Observability: we can expose a per-token latency dashboard (Prometheus/Grafana link) and a signed iframe for your SREs. We'll include the dashboard link in the SOW + a data retention clause (30 days for metrics).

I'll attach the SOW skeleton and the SLA wording. If procurement wants amortized billing, finance will need the pricing table per month — see Reserved_Nodes_Pricing_Table.xlsx (Jordan attached earlier).

I'll prepare a version of the amendment that includes the hot spare and the failover window (RTO 10 minutes for automated cross-region fallback).

— Karthik
VP, Solutions | Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: Latency-SLA-Draft.docx; Acme_SOW-2026Q4-dedicated-amendment.pdf (draft SOW)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@acme-retail.com>, Procurement Team <procure@acme-retail.com>

Date: Sun, 4 Oct 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Contract amendment: adding EU + APAC reserved pools (renewal window)

Sophie / Procurement —

Thanks for the timely feedback. Attached are the documents we discussed:
- Acme_SOW-2026Q4-dedicated-amendment.pdf (draft SOW with FRA-1 pinning and dashboard section)
- Reserved_Nodes_Pricing_Table.xlsx (monthly amortization rows added)
- DocuSign-Amendment-Acme.pdf (prepared to send)

Key points in the draft amendment:
- EU (FRA-1): 9 reserved A100-equivalent nodes (8 active + 1 hot spare)
- APAC (SGP): 7 reserved nodes (6 active + 1 hot spare)
- Baseline throughput guarantee: 70 concurrent sessions (EU) / 50 (APAC) measured at 95th percentile for 512-token requests; instrumentation via shared Grafana dashboard (link in SOW).
- Failover: automated cross-region fallback to US pool with RTO target of 10 minutes; fallbacks are billed at the baseline rate while fallback is in effect.
- Billing: monthly amortized invoice line items for the incremental capacity.

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached SOW and DocuSign packet.
2) If procurement approves, we will send real DocuSign envelopes (one amendment + one SOW) to procure@acme-retail.com.
3) Marissa will confirm any pricing concessions (cc'd).

If this looks OK I will send the DocuSign envelope first thing Monday morning so your legal/procurement team can begin routing.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_SOW-2026Q4-dedicated-amendment.pdf; Reserved_Nodes_Pricing_Table.xlsx; DocuSign-Amendment-Acme.pdf
